=== WIRE LAYOUTS (NetMessages.cs, comment block above NetCodec.CupState). u16 = two bytes low first; a nation/entrant of -1 is 0xFFFF / 255 ===
MsgType: CupState = 23 (host->clients, Reliable, HOST-ONLY), CupRequest = 24 (client->host, Reliable), CupStream = 25 (client->host->the spectators of that slot, Unreliable, RELAYED raw), CupRoundState = 26 (host->clients, Reliable, HOST-ONLY). ProtocolVersion stays 8 (new types, no changed layouts).
CupState (MsgType byte then): u8 version(=CupNet.StateVersion 1) | u32 tick (host Director.Tick) | u8 phase (CupPhase) | u32 phaseSerial | f32 phaseTime | u8 stage | u8 style | u8 format | u32 seed | u8 captainSlot | u16 teamNation | u8 leverPulls | u8 flags (1 = hasBracket) | u8 currentRound (stage<<5 | index, 255 none) | u8 nPlayers | nPlayers x PLAYER | u8 nOrder | nOrder x u8 slot | u8 nResults | nResults x RESULT | u32 bracketHash.
  PLAYER (15 B): u8 slot | u16 nation | u8 entrant (255 none) | u8 status (CupPlayerStatus: 1 Ready, 2 Out, 4 ReplacedByAi, 8 Left, 16 Loaded, 32 Playing, 64 Spectated) | u8 spectating (255 none) | u16 liveOpponent | u8 liveFor | u8 liveAgainst | u8 liveKick | u8 coin (CupCoinBits: 1 HasCall, 2 CallTails, 4 HasVerdict, 8 Right) | u8 coinMade | u8 coinRight.
  RESULT: u8 stage<<5|index | u8 flags (1 simulated, 2 suddenDeath, 4 firstKickerIsB) | [played only] u8 scoreA | u8 scoreB | u8 nKicks | ceil(nKicks/2) x u8 (KickRecord nibbles, two a byte). A simulated round is 2 bytes (seed-derivable: the client re-runs CupSim.Simulate(round, Bracket, CupSim.StreamFor(Bracket, round))).
  Vote counts are NOT sent (derived from the players' nations by RecountNationVotes). The draw is NOT sent (rebuilt: CupBracket.Build(seed, format, rows with entrant >= 0 as (nation, slot, name) - Co-op: (teamNation, captainSlot, YourTeam) -, CupNations.ResolvedPool())).
  SIZE: fixed 28 (incl. MsgType) + 15/player + 1 + order + 1 + results + 4. WORST CASE = 639 bytes: 8 players (120) + 8 order (9) + 23 human-involved rounds at 30 kicks (20 B each = 460) + 8 simulated (16) + hash; a finished 8-human cup with ~8-kick rounds ~386 B; a finished 2-player cup ~192 B. CupNet.SizeOf(msg) computes it; CupDirector.LastStateBytes holds the last sent size on the host.
CupRequest: u8 kind (CupRequestKind) | u32 arg | u32 payloadLen | payload (<= NetCodec.CupRequestMaxPayload 1024). Kinds: PickNation(arg=nation), Ready(arg 1/0), Spectate(arg=slot), Unspectate, RoundResult(payload=CupNet.PackRound: CupRound.WriteTo), Loaded, SetOrder(payload=CupNet.PackOrder), CallCoin(arg=(int)CoinFace), SkipCelebration, PullLever(9), CaptainDecides(10), Continue(11, refused: host-only), PlayAgain(12, refused: host-only), Quit(13), LiveRow(14, payload=CupNet.PackLiveRow: u16 opponentNation, u8 for, u8 against, u8 kick, u8 playing).
CupStream: u8 fromSlot (overwritten by the session with the sender's real slot) | u32 seq | v3 camPos | f32 x4 camRot (x,y,z,w) | f32 camFov | v3 ballPos | u16 nationA | u16 nationB | u8 nBodies (<= 32) | nBodies x BODY. BODY (21 B): u8 vslot (CupBody.VirtualSlot) | u8 slot (the human whose look it wears, 255 = AI/referee) | u8 flags (CupStreamBodyFlags: 1 SideB, 2 KeeperBody, 4 Referee) | v3 pos (pelvis, y = 0) | f32 yaw | u8 emoteId (255 none) | u8 emotePhase (0..255). 55 + 21n bytes.
CupRoundState: u32 len | len x u8 = CupRoundState.ToBytes() (its own versioned record; <= NetCodec.CupRoundStateMaxBytes 512; really <= 54 B) -> message <= 59 B.
Snapshot (existing MsgType.Snapshot, used for host-simulated rounds and the podium): BodyState.slot = CupBody.VirtualSlot (humans 0..7, twins/AI/referee 8..), pos = pelvis with y = 0, yaw = FacingRotation.eulerAngles.y, emoteId/emotePhase from the body's Celebration (255/0 idle), anim = AnimState hint (Dive/Down/Run/Idle), lastInputTick = session.InputTickForSlot(slot) for humans, erect from AnatomySim; tick = Director.Tick; homeScore/awayScore = ScoreA/ScoreB.

h.notesForNextAgents:
HEAD TO HEAD AGENT - exact calls. (1) Host flow only: everything below the host does through the ordinary intents/Apply* and SetPhase; the wire follows automatically (StateChanged -> CupState). A client's flow (the same partial running with IsAuthority false) MUST be driven by PHASE ENTRIES (PhaseSerial latch) only - the model it reads has been applied by CupDirector.Net before the entry fires - and must never SetPhase itself except through the host's echo. (2) NationPick: picks arrive as ApplyPick on the host (a refused race never echoes; the picker snaps back). (3) Loading, parallel phase: every peer with a human-vs-AI round this stage: StartRound(LocalRoundThisStage) (AuthorityFor -> Local), wait Driver.SceneBuilt, then NotifyLoaded(); the host advances when LoadBarrierOpen (AllLoaded or 10 s) -> SetPhase(CoinToss). Peers without a round (drawn against a human) wait for the head-to-head phase. (4) Round, parallel phase: call UpdateLiveRow() every tick (a CLIENT's row reaches the host through the automatic LiveRow request; the host's own row is local); at Driver.Phase == Over: RecordResult(CurrentRound, Driver.Line) then ReportRoundResult(CurrentRound) (a no-op on the host), RecordLocalRoundCareer, EndRound(). (5) Head-to-head phase, host: pick the pending human-vs-human round, StartRound(round) BEFORE SetPhase(Loading) so CupState carries currentRound; every OTHER peer's Loading entry: `var r = HostRound; if (r != null) StartRound(r)` (AuthorityFor gives Client on every non-host peer; a non-participant seated this way gets a Client driver whose puppets follow the snapshots - or leave non-participants in the lobby and let Spectate show them the round: the view builds its own puppets when no driver stands), then NotifyLoaded(). Both participants' rows read Playing (the host's from StartRound, the client's from its LiveRow report), which is what enables the lobby's Spectate button. (6) Coin toss in a host round: BeginCoinToss on EVERY peer; the official caller's call (a seeded side) reaches clients through the CupState echo of CupPlayer.CoinCall (within ~100 ms + RTT); EnsureCoinOutcome + RecordLocalCoinCall before Driver.Begin(); the host calls Driver.Begin() and SetPhase(Round); a client's driver Begin()s from the host's CupRoundState (ApplyState moves the phase) - do NOT call Driver.Begin() on a client. (7) The replay skip in a host round needs nothing from you (session SkipVote -> VoteSkipReplayBy; the HUD's click already calls VoteSkipReplay). (8) Spectate: the lobby's Spectate button -> Spectate(slot) (already wired in CupLobbyUI); the view appears on the echo and closes itself when the watched player stops Playing, on Esc, or when a round with a local body starts. Nothing else to do; if the lobby screen should hide while spectating, read director.Spectator != null. (9) Leavers: ApplyLeave runs on the host from RosterChanged or CupRequest.Quit; a leaver mid-round keeps their bodies (their NetInputSource goes stale: the taker auto-fires at the clock, the keeper stands) - if you want their side to play on with the bot, swap tb.NetInput for a CupBotTaker in the driver on ApplyLeave (Scene.cs InputForSlot territory). (10) Podium: enter it exactly as Solo (RecordResult, EndRound, SimulateAiRounds, CupCareer.Won, SetPhase(Podium), TryBeginPodium() in the entry); the champion's emote sync is automatic. Play Again on the host = PlayAgain() (ResetForNewCup + SetPhase(NationPick)); clients follow the seed change. End Match on the host = EndMatch() (Ended goes out first); clients leave on the echo by themselves. (11) `Ended` on a client is handled here (leave next tick) - leave the Ended case empty.
CO-OP AGENT: (1) The Captain is the host: SetOrder/PullLever/CaptainDecides are host-local intents and ride CupState (CoopOrder, LeverPulls, TeamNation); a client's CupOrderUI only reads them (the request kinds exist should a non-host Captain ever be wanted). (2) Every round is host-simulated: host StartRound(LocalRoundThisStage) before SetPhase(Loading); every client's Loading entry StartRound(HostRound ?? LocalRoundThisStage) (both name the same round in Co-op) then NotifyLoaded(); host gates on LoadBarrierOpen. (3) The trophy lift: at Over of a won Final on the host: RecordResult, RecordLocalRoundCareer, SimulateAiRounds, CupCareer.Won, SetPhase(TrophyLift), BeginTrophyLift() in the entry and NO EndRound before it - the host driver keeps publishing snapshots (the referee's Clap included) and feeding remote inputs past Over, and every client's driver keeps posing puppets and sending input, so the free window moves remote humans. Clients run BeginTrophyLift too (camera + UI only, `_simulates` false). (4) The calls band reads CupPlayer.CoinCall/CoinCallRight from the echo (ResolveCoinCalls runs on the host inside CupCoinToss). (5) GAME OVER / CHAMPIONS results: EndMatch()/PlayAgain() as above.
BOTH: never call Multiplayer.End() or touch the session from a flow; never Notify() from inside a GUI pass (the coalescer would send from OnGUI - harmless but avoid). CupState carries NO player names (the roster has them) and NO draw (rebuilt); if you add a replicated field, add it to CupStateMsg + NetCodec.CupState/ReadCupState + CupNet.BuildState + CupDirector.Net.NetApplyState, bump CupNet.StateVersion, and keep SizeOf honest.

First test: Multiplayer.UseDirectIp = false, two editors or a build + editor, a Head to Head lobby of two, watch CupState land (director.LastStateBytes on the host), a parallel round's live row in the other peer's lobby, Spectate on that row, then a human-vs-human round.

A client TAKER in a host-simulated round has no power meter: the client driver never arms a SetPieceTaker (CupHud reads driver.Taker.IsCharging/Meter). Fix in the Scene/Kick partial: a displayOnly SetPieceTaker.Begin on the local shooter body at OnStateApplied(Armed) with the local look-ray aim, exactly NetSetPieceMatch.ClientDriveTaker.

No client-side keeper prediction (the task's 'if feasible'): the twin swap, HoldLine and dive-on-the-host's-ball make a predicted keeper worth less than a puppet; the local keeper on a client moves a round trip late. NetSetPieceMatch's ReconcileLocalBody would need a live KeeperController on the client body (BuildBodies builds every client body as a puppet).

Client puppets are posed with DisplaySnap / DisplayEmote (C1's ApplyBodyPose): a running AI taker or a diving keeper reads as a sliding statue on a client. BodyState.anim carries the AnimState hint already; teaching ApplyBodyPose a DisplayAnim path (as NetSetPieceMatch does) is the fix.

A leaver mid-round in a host-simulated round keeps their bodies driven by a stale NetInputSource (design 10 says AI plays on): the kick clock's auto-shot and a standing keeper cover it, but the bot swap on ApplyLeave is not done (Scene.cs InputForSlot / CupBody.NetInput).

The client's rebuilt draw depends on CupNations.ResolvedPool() being identical on both builds; a mismatch is detected by the bracket hash and logged once, not repaired (the ProtocolVersion gate is the real guard; a nation-table change must bump it).

CupRoundState for a host round can arrive before a slow client's driver is Configured and is dropped; the 0.5 s resend covers it, and the Idle phase lasts through the loading card and the coin toss, so nothing is lost in practice - but a client that Configures more than ~10 s late joins from the first state it sees, as design 10 allows.

The spectator view's scoreboard shows only what the live row carries (opponent, score, kick number); the kick pips, the callouts and the kick clock of a spectated LOCAL round are not streamed (a participant of a HOST round bound with a Client driver gets the full CupHud instead).

i.notesForNextAgents:
1) PHASE SHAPE: a parallel wave is Loading -> Round on the host's clock; the CoinToss phase is used ONLY for host rounds (Interstitial -> Loading -> CoinToss -> Round). Each owner's toss in a wave runs under Round, which is why CallCoin (director + the host's request gate) accepts a call while Toss != null / in H2H's Round phase, and why H2HCursorAfterUnpause exists (CursorShouldBeFree says captured in Round). Do not move parallel tosses onto the CoinToss phase without re-checking those three seams.
2) COIN BOOKKEEPING in Head to Head: the host's own parallel call is judged by the ceremony (ResolveCoinCalls, localOnly); a remote owner's parallel call is judged by H2HResolveParallelCalls once their RoundResult lands (from the seeded face, never from the wire); a host round's calls (participants + watchers) are judged by the ceremony at the flip. H2HBeginToss clears only the local call for parallel tosses (BeginCoinToss's ClearCoinCalls would wipe other owners' pending calls). The career coin write comes from the ceremony's LocalPick captured in the onDone closure (RecordLocalCoinCall is not used here: the model's local CoinCall can be nulled by an echo mid-toss).
3) NON-PARTICIPANTS OF A HOST ROUND get a Client driver (puppets from the host's snapshots) plus an auto Spectate on the lower-slot participant for the camera (CupSpectatorView in camera-only mode) and a watch bar; Esc (the view's) frees the camera, H2HWatcherCamera then keeps GameCamera.Broadcast. During a parallel wave a peer without a round stays in the lobby and spectates through H's CupStream puppets - it cannot call the coin there (no ceremony without a driver); design 6.11's "a spectator already watching calls" holds for host rounds only.
4) THE WAVE BOOKKEEPING is host-only: _h2hWaveRounds (the CupRound objects from PendingRounds, mutated in place by SetResult), H2HWaveDone, the watchdog (HeadToHeadResultGrace after the owner's row stops Playing, HeadToHeadWaveCap absolute), and ApplyRoundResult now refusing a Done round so a late report cannot overwrite the sim. A leaver's round is simulated by SimulateAiRounds (their entrant is no longer IsHuman); a pending human-vs-human round that lost a human becomes a LATE WAVE from the lobby (H2HHostAdvance -> H2HStartWave(false)) - the host waits for the running wave to finish first (never re-opens Loading under running rounds).
5) STAGE GATE: ClearReady runs at the stage's FIRST wave (the pick's Ready would advance the first lobby at once); AdvanceStage already resets it for later stages. A player who finished early may press Ready while others play; it persists into the Lobby phase gate.
6) CLIENT CONCLUSION EDGE: a client's Over state and the host's next CupState can land in one poll, so H2HEndAnyRound (every non-wave entry) runs H2HClientRoundOver first for a standing client host-round driver (career round write + local RecordResult); H2HClientRoundOver itself never opens the lobby (the caller decides the screen) so a Podium / NationPick entry cannot leak one.
7) HandSlotToAi (CupRoundDriver.Leaver.cs) makes a leaver's side an AI side IN PLACE: CupBody.Slot -1 flips IsHuman, which every role lookup, the twin park rule, AnyHumanOn, CountHumansWithBodies and the choreography's human filters read; the KeeperController stays on the gloved body (Tick-driven only; TickKeeperOnLine prefers Ai) and the Striker stays on the shooter body (ControlEnabled false). Wire ids never change. It is called from H2HTickLeavers only for Host-authority rounds; Co-op could reuse it for a leaving shooter/keeper if the order rules allow.
8) The Kick.cs client Intro seam benefits Co-op clients too (they never captured the cursor either); CupHud's meter for a client TAKER is still missing (H's open issue: a displayOnly SetPieceTaker.Begin at OnStateApplied(Armed)).
9) The Co-op agent is editing CupDirector.cs / CupDirector.Net.cs / CupRoundDriver.Kick.cs concurrently (its ApplyLeave grew for the order collapse); my three seams were verified present at the end - re-check `grep -n "Toss == null) return\|bool localOnly\|late report ignored" CupDirector.cs`, `grep -n "HeadToHead && Phase == CupPhase.Round" CupDirector.Net.cs`, `grep -n _clientIntroShown CupRoundDriver.Kick.cs` after its pass.

j.notesForNextAgents:
1) CLIENT FLOW RULE (kept exactly as H specified): CupDirector.Coop.cs never SetPhase()s on a client; every client action hangs off a phase ENTRY (PhaseSerial latch) or a poll of data the host echoed (CurrentRound.Done for the career write, the players' Left flags for leavers, LeverPulls for the reel). If you add a Co-op beat, put its client half in CoopEnter or a watcher, never in the tick's host branches.
2) PARTIAL ORDERS ARE A MODEL STATE NOW: CoopOrder may hold -1 entries between the Bracket and Loading phases. Anything that consumes CoopOrder must check CupDirector.CoopOrderComplete first (MakeRoundSetup does; CupStatsLedger.Reconstruct reads the stage's carried-over order, which is complete by then). On the wire an empty entry is CupNet.EmptyOrderSlot (255) - use CupNet.OrderSlotByte/OrderSlotFromByte, never a bare clamp.
3) ApplyOrder now un-readies everyone on a REAL change (identical orders are ignored). RollOrder still bumps LeverPulls even when the shuffle lands on the current order (a 1-player team), so the reel plays and the gate waits CoopReelSeconds. LeverPulls is deliberately never reset per stage (the salt CupSalts.Order(stage) + 16 * pulls stays unique for stage < 16; a reset could be coalesced away with the first pull on a client); ResetForNewCup still zeroes it.
4) The starting order of every stage after the first is the previous stage's (collapsed for leavers) so a settled team is one Ready away; the first stage starts all-empty. CoopKeeperLeft is the Captain's prompt only (host-local, not on the wire); it is cleared when the next round starts.
5) LEAVERS: the director does not call the driver from ApplyLeave. CoopWatchLeavers sees a player's Left flag rise on EVERY peer and calls CupRoundDriver.HumanLeft(slot) while a round stands, so the host and every client retire / re-slot the same bodies. Head to Head's HandSlotToAi (CupRoundDriver.Leaver.cs, agent I) is a separate bot swap; the two do not overlap (HumanLeft only re-slots in Co-op). The re-slotted gloves keep the leaver's LOOK (the body is not rebuilt) and their VirtualSlot (the wire id stays the body's) - only Slot/Name/input change.
6) A body with CupBody.Gone must be treated like a parked twin everywhere: skipped in placements and marks, never a voter, never a coin-toss captain. If you add a loop over _bodies that moves or counts humans, add `|| b.Gone` beside the `b.Parked` test.
7) The client-side Begin duties (cursor capture, intro card) now live in ApplyClientCamera guarded by `_clientBegun`; do not add a second CaptureCursor(true) on the client path or the Over release (`_cursorCaptured`) gets out of step.
8) On a client the coin-toss onDone can land in the Round phase (its ceremony starts a round trip late): CoopConsumeToss is called from both the CoinToss and Round ticks. Do not move RecordLocalCoinCall back into the CoinToss tick only.
9) The host's loading card waits for LoadBarrierOpen; a client's card waits for the host's CoinToss phase (the CoinToss entry hides it), so a slow peer never watches an empty pitch and a late client starts its round from the CoinToss / Round / TrophyLift entry (CoopEnsureRoundStarted) rather than never.
10) Pause labels per role were already in place (GameBootstrap.BuildMode: host "End Match" / "Ends the cup for everyone", client "Quit to Menu" / "You are dropped from the order"; PauseMenu.Overlay true) - verified, not changed.

r1.notesForNextAgents:
1) THE FIRST LOOPBACK TEST is still owed (no editor / MCP per the brief): `Multiplayer.UseDirectIp = false`, two editors or a build + editor, a Head to Head lobby of two. Watch in order: director.LastStateBytes on the host after the pick (~60-200 B), the parallel wave (both loading cards, both tosses under the Round phase, live rows in the other peer's lobby, Spectate on the playing row -> CupStream puppets on the watcher), the Round of 16 human-vs-human round (interstitial on both; the client gets ONE intro card now, its cursor captured, its power meter sweeping while it charges - the display taker - and its release landing on the host's body a round trip later), a client Quit mid-host-round (HandSlotToAi arms the bot), Play Again from the podium (the seed changes, both peers back to CHOOSE YOUR NATION, the podium's emote cursor reset), and End Match from the host (clients reach the main menu through the Ended echo, never 'connection lost'). Then one Co-op stage: the client's career round write must land on the Bracket entry (it did not before), a client keeper diving on the host's ball a round trip late, the trophy lift's free window moving a remote human.
2) VALIDATION CONTRACTS added on the host: (a) RoundResult must name a round with AuthorityFor == Local and a first kicker that follows from the seeded coin + the OWNER's own call as the host holds it (CupPlayer.CoinCall; HEADS when null). A client's CallCoin request always precedes its RoundResult on the same reliable stream, so the host's copy is current; if you ever move parallel tosses off the Round phase, keep the host's CallCoin request gate (CupDirector.Net, the CallCoin case) accepting them or every parallel result will be refused and simulated. (b) A changed call now clears its verdict (ApplyCoinCall) - do not rely on CoinCallRight surviving a re-call. (c) Replay-skip votes count only slots with a body; CupHud's CanVoteReplay already matches.
3) CLIENT TAKER METER: `_taker` on a Client driver is the display-only taker. ArmTaker (host/local) and ClientSyncDisplayTaker (client) both use `_chargeGate`; they never coexist on one driver. If ApplyBodyPose ever grows a DisplayAnim path, the display taker's run-up pose writes still land on kinematic bones and are overridden by the snapshot every frame - it is meter-only by design.
4) A CLIENT'S PUPPET BODY MUST NEVER GET Celebration.Play: the HUD and the lift now pass a null Celebration on a client; the podium's winner is a LIVE body on every peer (CupPodium builds it), so that wheel keeps its local Play. Keep that split if you add another wheel.
5) IsAuthority is now false on a client whose session died until GameBootstrap.OnHostConnectionLost tears the match down (`_netLostAsClient`). A flow that wants to react to the host vanishing should watch `NetBound` flipping false, not IsAuthority.
6) The Co-op client's career latch (`_coopCareerWritten`) is reset at the Round entry and consumed by CoopClientRoundConcluded from whichever tick or entry first sees CurrentRound.Done - the host's result and its next phase arrive in ONE CupState (the coalescer only flushes from NetTick; a SetPhase forces one), so a Round-phase poll alone was never enough. Head to Head already had the same edge covered by H2HEndAnyRound -> H2HClientRoundOver.
7) A client now FOLLOWS a host-simulated verdict over its own played result (NetApplyResult): its bracket, lobby row and later stages agree with the host; only the career line it already wrote for that round keeps the client's own numbers (accepted).
8) Unchanged and worth knowing: CupRoundState.CoinResult and CupResultRow.firstKicker do cross the wire; the face is seed-derived but the first kicker depends on a human's call, so the row must carry it. CupStream is deliberately NOT in IsHostOnly (clients send it); its direction checks are inline in RouteMessage. NetSession.SlotOf stays private; the relay table is the only slot->slot fact the session keeps for the cup.

No client-side keeper prediction (H's open issue, unchanged and deliberate): a client's keeper is a puppet answering the host a round trip later; NetSetPieceMatch's ReconcileLocalBody would need a live KeeperController on the client body.

Client puppets are posed with DisplaySnap / DisplayEmote only: a running AI taker or a diving keeper reads as a sliding statue on a client. BodyState.anim carries the AnimState hint already; teaching ApplyBodyPose a DisplayAnim path (as NetSetPieceMatch does) is the fix.

Esc on a LOBBY spectator's view (CupSpectatorView, a locally simulated round watched through CupStream) closes the view only on the host's echo (~RTT); until then CupEscape.Owned keeps the pause menu from opening on that press. A local clear of LocalPlayer.SpectatingSlot would be re-applied by the next stale CupState, so it was left on the echo; a 'pending unspectate' latch in NetApplyPlayers (like the coin call's) would make it instant.

The host's EndMatch sends CupState(Ended) as one reliable UDP packet and shuts the socket immediately (no ack wait); a lost packet leaves a client on the 5 s host timeout -> HostConnectionLost -> main menu (correct, just slower). Same for a client's CupRequest.Quit: the host then learns of the leave from the peer timeout.

The Co-op reel gate and the lever landing (agent J's note) and the display taker's meter rate against the host's real taker are untested for feel: the client's meter sweeps on its own clock from its own Space, the host's from the wire input ~RTT later, so the client sees its release before the host's body swings - the same offset NetSetPieceMatch has.
